drivers.why_material: The company labeled 'Mean Change from Baseline in Hyperphagia at Visit 7' as the 'Primary Endpoint' in marketing materials for the catalyst trial NCT03714373, when the registered co-primaries are actually safety/AEs and 'Change from RW Period Baseline in HQ-CT Total Score' at Week 16. This is direct misrepresentation of the success-determining endpoint for this specific catalyst readout.

Marketing emphasized CGI-I as a 'Key Secondary Endpoint' when the registered primary efficacy endpoint is HQ-CT Total Score. This de-emphasis of the actual primary in favor of a secondary is a classic signal that the company expects the registered primary to underperform.

Similarly positioned body fat mass (DXA) as a 'Key Secondary Endpoint' while downplaying the registered primary (HQ-CT). The pattern of elevating multiple secondaries over the registered primary suggests masking of expected primary endpoint weakness.

dismissed.why_not_material: Per principle #3, this is open-label extension data (C601/C602) presented alongside the controlled pivotal trial. While the finding is severe for evidence quality, citing uncontrolled OLE data as supportive color when the catalyst is a controlled Phase 3 is standard biotech promotion, not masking of the catalyst trial itself.
Same as slno_022—open-label extension data presented as context, not misrepresentation of the catalyst trial design or expected results.
Same as slno_022—OLE data at week 39, standard IR practice for context around a controlled pivotal.
Same as slno_022—OLE data at week 52, promotional context not catalyst masking.
Open-label behavioral data from C601/C602 extension. Standard supportive promotion for a Phase 3 catalyst.
Exposure-response claim from OLE data. While uncontrolled, this is typical pharmacometric analysis presented as supportive context, not misrepresentation of the blinded catalyst trial.

Cross-trial comparison to PATH natural history is minor severity; while methodologically weak, it's common in rare disease contexts and does not directly mask the catalyst trial's own design or expected outcome.
Same as slno_026—cross-study benchmark, minor severity, not direct catalyst masking.
Biomarker data (leptin, insulin, HOMA-IR, adiponectin) from OLE; moderate severity but presented as exploratory/mechanistic context, not as the catalyst success criterion.
Exposure-response for biomarkers; moderate severity but exploratory, not endpoint substitution for the catalyst.
Timeline guidance minor mismatch (Q3 vs. registered Q2). Minor severity operational drift, not indicative of data quality masking.

analyst_note: Soleno systematically misrepresented the primary endpoint of the Phase 3 catalyst trial NCT03714373 in pre-readout marketing. The company labeled hyperphagia change at Visit 7 as the 'Primary Endpoint' in investor materials when the registered co-primaries are safety/AEs and the HQ-CT Total Score at Week 16. Concurrently, marketing elevated CGI-I and body fat mass—both registered secondaries—as 'Key Secondary Endpoints,' a classic tell that management expects the actual registered primary (HQ-CT) to miss or underperform. This is direct, severe endpoint manipulation specific to the catalyst trial, not merely promotional spin around open-label extension data (which we dismiss as normal IR). The endpoint shell game is a red flag for masking a likely miss on the registered primary at topline.
